slides.title: S7900 odd-form insertion with lead clinching for 5 SPD boards
slides.subtitle: One 6-head S7900 with a 15-layer tray feeder and customised grippers inserts two bulky SPD modules and clinches every lead before wave soldering.
slides.notes: Southern Machinery odd-form insertion automation proposal, 2026 (customer, part numbers, prices removed).

slides.title: From conveyor to clinched, solder-ready board

steps.b: Inlet conveyor brings the board or fixture into the S7900; board in and out takes 4 s, mark recognition 1 s.
Six heads with customised grippers pick SPD modules from a 15-layer tray feeder: 0.3 s pick, 0.3 s insert per part.
Each lead is bent 15–30° under the board right after insertion, 1.5 s per part, so parts cannot float in the wave.
Outlet conveyor passes the board to wave soldering through a SMEMA interface.

slides.caption: S7900 6-head odd-form insertion machine

slides.title: Five boards, two bulky SPD modules
slides.note: PCB sizes given: Board 1 233 × 139 mm, Board 3 382 × 330 mm (panel). Others to be confirmed.

slides.title: 30 – 59 boards an hour with every lead clinched
slides.note: Cycle = rounds × (6 × 0.3 s pick + 1.8 s head move + 6 × 0.3 s insert) + 1.5 s clinch per part + 4 s board in/out + 1 s marks. Board 4 without clinch: 3,600 ÷ 32 s gives 112, the proposal states 105; to be confirmed.
slides.notes: Southern Machinery odd-form insertion automation proposal, 2026 (customer, part numbers, prices removed).

slides.title: Up to 79 % more boards an hour than the current benchmark
slides.text: Without clinching, the S7900 runs Board 1 at 147 boards an hour against 82 and Board 3 at 96 against 63 on the reference machine. Configuration: 1 × S7900 6-head core machine, 1 × STF248E tray feeder, 6 × customised 24JD04L49 grippers.
slides.notes: Comparison table in the proposal; Board 1 detailed calculation gives 145. Concept view.

slides.title: Why the tray feeder wins for bulky SPD modules
slides.note: Boards per refill: Board 1 90 vs 38.85, Board 2 94.5 vs 40.8, Board 3 70 vs 29, Board 4 84 vs 35, Board 5 52 vs 22 (theoretical).

slides.title: Clinched leads keep SPD modules flat through the wave
bullets: Automatic lead bending of about 15–30° right after insertion.
Clinch length 1.3–1.8 mm under the board.
Outward bend, inner bend, circular and 2-turn patterns.
Stops component floating during wave soldering and keeps modules vertical.
Adds 1.5 s per part to the cycle, shown in the clinch columns.
slides.caption: Lead clinching unit and bend patterns

slides.title: S7900 key specifications
rows: 2 top mark CCD + 4 bottom component CCD
Nozzle / clamp; up to 18 feeder stations
slides.note: One slide of the proposal lists a 4-head version at 1100 × 1500 × 1700 mm; the 6-head version is used here.

slides.title: Feeding and handling around the S7900
bullets: Customised balanced tray feeder: dual drive at 0.5–0.8 MPa, 2000 W, buttons and screen.
Handles SMDs, small passives and odd-shaped parts, with alarms and maintenance prompts.
15-layer magazine of 450 × 300 mm trays.
Inlet and outlet conveyors: 900 ± 20 mm height, left to right by default, 75 kg.
3 mm ESD flat belt, PCB 0.4–4.0 mm, fixture 1.0–10.0 mm, ±0.2 mm stop repeatability, SMEMA.
slides.caption: Tray feeder magazine loaded with trays

slides.title: What the parts, boards and trays need
bullets: Leads 0.5 × 7 mm bend easily and cannot be modified: handle with the gripper and tray design.
Widen board holes from 1.2 × 10.2 mm to 2.4 × 10.2 mm for more insertion tolerance.
All pins in one orientation to avoid pick-up interference.
Tray: width 150–340 mm, depth 90–230 mm, height 5–36 mm, 500 g including parts.
≥5 mm from divider top to part top; ≥5 mm gap in the gripper closing direction.
Part-to-grid gap within 0.5 mm, burr-free walls, long side across the tray.
